small_guidance:
- The output spatial M = 30·62·62 = 115320 is large; bias toward BLOCK_M=64 or 128 with BLOCK_N=32 (OC=32 fits one tile, eliminating the OC grid dim entirely). Add a config `(128, 32, 32)` and `(64, 32, 32)` at num_warps=4, stages=2 and 3 — these should better amortize the weight load across M.
- Since OC=32 exactly, drop the pid_oc grid axis and hardcode BLOCK_N≥32 so the autotune key only sweeps M tiling; this removes a redundant mask and lets the compiler hoist weight loads.
- The K dimension is IC·KD·KH·KW = 8·27 = 216 — quite small. Try BLOCK_K=32 or 54 (a divisor) and unroll the K-loop; with K so small, increasing num_stages to 3-4 on a smaller-SMEM tile may help hide the gather latency.
large_guidance:
- Reformulate so each program handles a full (N, OC=32) tile at one output (d,h,w) tile: since OC is tiny, treat OC as the inner accumulator dimension and tile only over (N·OD·OH·OW). Load the entire weight tensor (32·216·4B = 27KB) once into SMEM/registers per program-group via a persistent/2D grid, eliminating repeated weight reloads.
- Consider an NHWDC (channels-last) layout: permute input to (N, OD, OH, OW, IC) and weights to (KD·KH·KW·IC, OC) so the K-dimension gather becomes contiguous IC-vectorized loads. This usually beats im2col-gather for small IC.
- Alternatively, switch to a direct-conv formulation with the (kd,kh,kw) loop unrolled (only 27 iterations) and IC as the GEMM-K, with output tile (BLOCK_HW, OC=32). This avoids the implicit-im2col index arithmetic per K-step and gives cleaner coalesced loads.
